chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Mu'awiya ibn Hakam, from Sulayman ibn Muhammad al-Kha'thami, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the distance at which shortening of prayer is performed, so he said, 'In a Baramil; woe to them, as if they had not performed Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so they shortened [the prayer].'

key_terms.وَيْحَهُمْ: Woe to them (an expression of warning or rebuke)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific distance for shortening prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the distance for shortening prayer (qasr) as one Baramil, using the phrase 'woe to them' to highlight the spiritual negligence of those who pray fully despite the concession. This comparison to those who neglected Hajj with the Prophet underscores the gravity of ignoring established religious easings (rukhas), a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding the balance between obligation and mercy. The narration is found in Chapter 23 of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, which systematically details the rules of prayer during travel.
